hints: Focus on where the three-carbon skeleton ends up in each reaction, in the acid part or the alcohol part.
Remember that a carboxylate salt plus a strong acid gives the free carboxylic acid back by protonation.
Check the ester hydrolysis options carefully to see which fragment becomes the acid and whether alkaline conditions leave it as a salt.
walkthrough:
**Recall how to make a free carboxylic acid**

Think of a carboxylic acid as $\text{RCOOH}$. You can get it by protonating its salt $\text{RCOO}^-$, by hydrolysing an ester or nitrile in acid, or by oxidising a primary alcohol or aldehyde.

Key rule:
$$\text{RCOO}^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$

**Test the salt plus acid route**

Ammonium propanoate contains the propanoate ion, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$. Dilute sulfuric acid supplies $\text{H}^+$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
That product is propanoic acid directly, with no heating or further steps needed.

**Check why the others do not give propanoic acid**

Alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl propanoate stops at sodium propanoate, oxidation of propan-2-ol stops at propanone, and acid hydrolysis of propyl ethanoate gives ethanoic acid. Only the salt plus dilute acid route gives free propanoic acid.

options.A: Ammonium propanoate provides $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$. Dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ protonates it to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which is propanoic acid. This is the standard salt of a weak acid plus strong acid displacement.
options.B: Heating ethyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, with aqueous NaOH is alkaline hydrolysis. It gives sodium propanoate plus ethanol, not the free acid. You would need a second step of acidification to get propanoic acid.
options.C: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. Strong oxidation with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ under reflux gives the ketone propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. Secondary alcohols cannot be oxidised to carboxylic acids because there is no further oxidisable C-H on that carbon.
options.D: Propyl ethanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Acid hydrolysis splits it into the acid from the acyl part and the alcohol from the alkyl part. Here that is ethanoic acid plus propan-1-ol, so the acid formed has two carbons, not three.
